extracted.intended_audience: general readers, fans, journalists, or researchers seeking an overview of comedian Daniel Tosh
extracted.subtask_description: A Wikipedia-style biographical profile summarizing Daniel Tosh's background, career, comedic style, major works, controversies, and reception. Useful for understanding the comedian's genres, media formats, and public impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genres of comedy
rubrics_metrics.description: Lists the kinds of comedy the performer practices: Observational comedy; black comedy; insult comedy; cringe comedy; shock humor; sarcasm; satire.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These genre labels indicate the stylistic approaches and expectations of the act (e.g., observational focuses on everyday life; shock humor aims to provoke). Use them to classify material and anticipate audience reactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subjects/themes addressed
rubrics_metrics.description: Common subjects the comedian addresses include: everyday life, human behavior, social awkwardness, sex, gender differences, racism, current events, pop culture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subject choices shape tone and risk level; sensitive subjects (racism, sex, gender, rape) may provoke controversy and require consideration of context and audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance media/platforms
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary media listed for career work: stand-up and television (also podcasts, specials, voice work, film appearances).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Medium affects format and constraints — e.g., stand-up allows longer monologue-driven sets; television may require segments or tighter editing; podcasts use conversational formats and recurring release schedules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deliberately offensive and controversial style
rubrics_metrics.description: Tosh is described as having a 'deliberately offensive and controversial style of black comedy' and 'mocking humor' that is 'envelope pushing.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This labels an intentional creative choice to provoke or transgress norms. It signals trade-offs: it can generate attention and a loyal audience but risks backlash, public debate, and reputational consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of punchlines and comedic voice
rubrics_metrics.description: Punchlines frequently are intentionally self-deprecating, racist, sexist, or homophobic; Tosh explains: 'I'm not a misogynistic and racist person...But I do find those jokes funny, so I say them.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This criterion describes voice and rhetorical stance — using taboo or prejudiced material as a comedic device. It is an evaluative axis for critics and audiences assessing intent, taste, and impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show format: Tosh.0 (clip-based commentary)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tosh.0 is described as 'a showcase of popular Internet video clips with the addition of Tosh's narrative comedic dialogue.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a production/format standard: curate viral clips and layer host commentary. Success depends on clip selection, host framing, and timing of jokes; legal/ethical issues (fair use, respect for subjects) may matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Career milestones as success indicators
rubrics_metrics.description: Key career milestones cited include: performance on Late Show with David Letterman (2001), Comedy Central Presents special, multiple stand-up specials, hosting Tosh.0 (2009–2020), appearances on national talk shows, festival 'New Faces' (Just for Laughs), and sold-out tours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appearances on high-profile shows, network specials, festival recognition, and commercial indicators (sold-out tours, Forbes earnings) are used as empirical measures of professional success and influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Controversy and appropriateness sensitivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Example: 2012 interaction where Tosh told jokes about rape and responded to an audience member by saying it would be funny if she were raped by 'five guys,' prompting lengthy debate over the appropriateness of rape jokes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Content that targets highly sensitive topics can trigger public debate and criticism. This criterion flags ethical boundaries, potential audience harm, and the likelihood of sustained media scrutiny.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commercial/reception metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Reception data referenced include viewership numbers for specials (e.g., Daniel Tosh: Happy Thoughts had 3.25 million viewers and a 1.9/5 share), Forbes' net worth/earnings rankings, average ticket price and sold-out tour statistics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use quantitative metrics (viewers, ticket sales, rankings, prices) to evaluate market success, reach, and profitability; these are separate from artistic or critical appraisal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Podcast production format
rubrics_metrics.description: Tosh Show podcast uses a common podcast format featuring guests in studio, a behind-the-camera contributor who chimes in, and video clips from the internet; episodes released weekly (every Tuesday).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standards for podcasting include consistent release cadence, guest selection, conversational dynamics, and incorporation of multimedia elements to retain audience engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Roles beyond performance (creative production credits)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tosh has credits as co-creator, writer, and executive producer (e.g., Brickleberry), and voice actor on animated shows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluating a comedian's career may include their creative/production contributions (creating shows, writing, producing), indicating breadth of industry involvement beyond onstage performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Philanthropy and benefit shows
rubrics_metrics.description: Tosh has hosted benefit shows (e.g., 'Tosh Saves The World') with proceeds going to charities and participated in shows for families of deceased comedians and disaster relief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participation in charity events is a dimension of professional reputation and public contribution; inclusion of high-profile guest lineups or recurring benefit events can enhance goodwill.
